evidence: `fando-plan/scripts/codex_lm.py` imports `verify_codex_cli` from `fando-plan/scripts/call_codex.py`, but still performs its own separate `codex exec` subprocess orchestration and error contract.

`fando-plan/scripts/call_codex.py`, `fando-plan/scripts/codex_lm.py`, `fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py`, and `fando-verify/scripts/gather_implementation.py` each own direct subprocess integration logic (command construction, timeout behavior, stderr handling) without a shared boundary module.

External-tool coupling policy is fragmented: git probing and codex probing are implemented in per-script helpers with different failure contracts (return-value errors vs raised runtime errors vs process exits), increasing change ripple when CLI behavior changes.

`fando-plan/scripts/call_codex.py` serves both as reusable library (`verify_codex_cli`, `call_codex`) and executable CLI (`main`), and `codex_lm.py` depends on it as a module; this blends entrypoint and reusable-layer responsibilities.

`fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py` and `fando-verify/scripts/gather_implementation.py` follow the same mixed pattern (domain logic + presentation/CLI printing + process exit behavior in one file), so ownership boundaries are not consistently separated by role.
The same architectural pattern repeats across both `fando-plan` and `fando-verify` script sets, indicating a systemic decomposition choice rather than an isolated file issue.

fando-plan/scripts/backfill_training.py defines reusable helpers (`classify_domain`, `parse_zellij_bridge`, `parse_jj_workspace`) that depend on globals (`PROFILES`, `ReviewExample`) only imported inside `main()` (lines 29, 43, 121 vs 207-208), unlike sibling scripts with module-level imports.

Both fando-plan/scripts/backfill_training.py and fando-plan/scripts/collect_training.py mutate `sys.path` at runtime in `main()` to enable local imports (backfill line 205, collect line 23), while sibling modules (`call_codex.py`, `codex_lm.py`, `optimize.py`) use standard import patterns.

Codex execution errors use incompatible contracts across adjacent paths: `call_codex.call_codex()` returns `CodexResult.error` strings (fando-plan/scripts/call_codex.py:69-138), while `CodexLM.forward()` raises RuntimeError for similar failures (fando-plan/scripts/codex_lm.py:93-103), and `run_dspy_review()` stores raw exceptions into result values (fando-plan/scripts/dspy_reviewers.py:457-464).

`load_optimized_module()` swallows all failures with `except Exception: return None` (fando-plan/scripts/dspy_reviewers.py:786-791), so callers like fando-plan/scripts/optimize.py cannot distinguish 'file missing' from 'state corrupt/incompatible'.

fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py uses broad `except Exception` for file reads (lines 151-152, 159-160) and string-based error returns, while other scripts often raise or hard-exit; failure behavior is not predictable at integration boundaries.

The training-data seam is brittle because parser helpers in fando-plan/scripts/backfill_training.py rely on runtime setup in `main()` rather than explicit parameters/imports, so the same functions are unsafe to call from other modules/tests.

Codex invocation is orchestrated through overlapping layers with different boundary behavior (`call_codex.py` command wrapper, `codex_lm.py` subprocess wrapper, `dspy_reviewers.py` exception-to-result conversion), creating handoff ambiguity for callers.
Optimization loading path (`optimize.py` -> `dspy_reviewers.load_optimized_module`) has no explicit outcome signal for corrupted state, so orchestration silently degrades to baseline modules.

fando-plan/scripts/aggregate_findings.py builds `unique_findings` for de-duplication (lines 194-205) but intentionally keeps `all_findings` unchanged (line 206), so a core abstraction step is computed but not applied.

The module-level contract says it "Merge[s] and analyze[s] findings", but output still contains duplicates in `all_findings` and totals (lines 319-347), increasing indirection cost without behavior gain.
fando-plan/scripts/run_parallel_reviews.py emits reviewer findings that are later aggregated; because dedup is not materialized, downstream consumers inherit duplicated signal.

fando-plan/scripts/dspy_reviewers.py hard-codes persistent state under `~/.claude/skills/fando-plan` (lines 41-43), introducing an undeclared runtime dependency on an external skill install path rather than repository-local state.
fando-plan/scripts/run_parallel_reviews.py defaults `--backend` to `dspy` (lines 379-383), so the non-local dependency path is on the default execution path when DSPy is present.
This setup increases environment drift risk across machines/CI because optimized/training artifacts are resolved outside repo boundaries.
fando-plan/scripts/run_parallel_reviews.py gracefully handles empty profiles in codex path (`if not profiles: return result`, lines 200-201).

fando-plan/scripts/dspy_reviewers.py sets `max_workers = len(profiles)` when unspecified (line 424) and immediately constructs `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers)` (line 454), which raises when `profiles` is empty.
Two neighboring execution paths for the same concept (parallel review) diverge in basic guard behavior, creating avoidable runtime fragility.

holistic_context.structure.directory_profiles shows `fando-plan/scripts/` has 12 files (threshold >10) with mixed responsibilities in one flat folder: aggregation (`aggregate_findings.py`), model-calling (`call_codex.py`), and training backfill (`backfill_training.py`).

`fando-plan/scripts/` and `fando-verify/scripts/` both report avg_fan_in=0.0 and avg_fan_out=0.0 in the packet structure profile, indicating script-only placement instead of explicit importable package boundaries.

Assigned files combine reusable functions and CLI entrypoints in the same modules (`main()` plus library-like helpers such as `aggregate_findings`, `parse_zellij_bridge`, `gather_diff`, `parse_verification`), which blurs placement by ownership.
Assigned scripts are heavily subprocess/git/filesystem dependent (`subprocess.run` in all four Python files) but expose no built-in seam for deterministic contract testing.
No test harness or quality-gate references are present in README for validating compatibility policy (for example Codex CLI version/support matrix) or plan/diff detection behavior.

`find_plan.py` and `gather_implementation.py` implement branch/path/error fallback logic that is risk-prone, but there is no evidence in reviewed scope of integration tests covering repo states (no remote, detached HEAD, missing base branch, empty diff).

Multiple scripts combine reusable domain logic and CLI side effects in the same file (e.g., run_parallel_reviews.py has orchestration plus argparse/printing/exit handling; dspy_reviewers.py has domain signatures, optimization/training persistence helpers, and CLI; aggregate_findings.py and parse_* scripts follow same pattern).

Parallel review orchestration exists in two separate flows with duplicated counting/result-shaping logic (run_parallel_reviews() and run_parallel_reviews_dspy() in run_parallel_reviews.py), increasing drift risk when adding fields or changing aggregation semantics.

Domain taxonomy and behavior are split across independently-maintained registries (detect_profiles.PROFILES vs dspy_reviewers.DOMAIN_SIGNATURES), while backfill_training.py classification relies on PROFILES; this creates structural coupling through duplicated constants rather than a single domain model.

Multiple scripts repeat near-identical CLI scaffolding (argparse setup, stdin read/empty check, --format text/json branching, sys.exit handling) in parse_findings.py, parse_verification.py, detect_profiles.py, detect_security_level.py, secrets.py, find_plan.py, and gather_implementation.py.

Several files include large boilerplate usage/output docstrings and explanatory comments that restate straightforward control flow rather than documenting non-obvious constraints (e.g., parse_findings.py, parse_verification.py, detect_profiles.py, detect_security_level.py, run_parallel_reviews.py).
codex_lm.py defines async aforward() that directly calls sync forward() without async subprocess or executor handoff, adding API ceremony with no behavioral gain.

codex_lm.py constructs OpenAI-style response metadata and token counts using split()-based estimates even though downstream return is [output_text], indicating template-style overconstruction not tied to actual contract usage.

findings.summary: CLI integration is duplicated across modules instead of centralized behind one adapter boundary.
evidence: `call_codex.py` and `codex_lm.py` both orchestrate `codex exec` subprocess calls with separate command assembly and error mapping.
`find_plan.py` and `gather_implementation.py` each implement their own subprocess invocation patterns for git with local timeout/error semantics.
No shared execution/policy layer exists for subprocess-backed tooling, so behavior diverges by script and creates broad ripple when external CLI contracts change.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared infrastructure module (for example, `scripts/lib/cli_exec.py`) that standardizes subprocess execution, timeout defaults, and structured error mapping, then have all four scripts consume that boundary rather than owning ad-hoc subprocess policy.

findings.summary: Script files mix reusable domain logic with CLI entrypoint behavior, blurring ownership boundaries.
evidence: `codex_lm.py` imports `verify_codex_cli` from `call_codex.py`, which is primarily a CLI script with `main()` and process-exit concerns.
`find_plan.py` and `gather_implementation.py` embed reusable discovery/diff logic and CLI formatting/exit handling in the same modules.
This repeated pattern across both subsystems makes top-level roles less explicit (entrypoint vs service logic), increasing coupling and reducing decomposition clarity.
findings.suggestion: Split each script into role-specific modules: keep thin CLI entrypoints (`main` + argparse + output) and move reusable logic into import-safe service modules (e.g., `plan_locator.py`, `git_diff_service.py`, `codex_service.py`) with consistent non-exiting return/exception contracts.

findings.summary: Backfill/collection scripts use inconsistent script-only import conventions that break module reuse.
evidence: fando-plan/scripts/backfill_training.py references `PROFILES` and `ReviewExample` in top-level helpers (lines 29, 43, 121) but imports them only inside `main()` (lines 207-208).
Both backfill and collect scripts prepend `Path(__file__).parent` to `sys.path` inside `main()` to make imports work, while sibling scripts are import-stable without path mutation.
findings.suggestion: Refactor these scripts to standard module imports at file scope (or pass dependencies explicitly into helper functions), and remove `sys.path` mutation so helpers are callable from tests and other modules.

findings.summary: Codex-related modules expose conflicting failure contracts (return-error, raise, and embed-exception).
evidence: `call_codex.call_codex()` returns `CodexResult(error=...)` on timeout/not-found/nonzero exit, while `CodexLM.forward()` raises RuntimeError for the same classes of failures.
`run_dspy_review()` catches all exceptions from worker futures and stores exception objects in `results[profile]`, and `prediction_to_review_output()` later stringifies them into summary text.
findings.suggestion: Define one shared error contract for Codex execution (e.g., typed exception hierarchy or a typed Result object) and enforce it across `call_codex`, `codex_lm`, and `dspy_reviewers` so callers can handle failures uniformly.

findings.summary: Optimized-module load path silently suppresses corruption/incompatibility errors.
evidence: fando-plan/scripts/dspy_reviewers.py:790-791 catches `Exception` and returns `None` without logging or reason.
fando-plan/scripts/optimize.py relies on load behavior during orchestration; silent fallback masks broken saved state and makes optimization effectiveness hard to diagnose.
findings.suggestion: Catch specific load exceptions, log the cause (or return structured error metadata), and distinguish 'not found' from 'invalid/corrupt module state' so orchestration can fail fast or warn clearly.

findings.summary: Backfill parsing functions depend on hidden global setup instead of explicit boundary inputs.
evidence: `parse_zellij_bridge()` / `parse_jj_workspace()` construct `ReviewExample` and call `classify_domain()` which depends on global `PROFILES`, but neither dependency is provided in function signatures.
The only place those dependencies are initialized is entrypoint-side imports in `main()`, coupling orchestration order to function correctness.
findings.suggestion: Make seams explicit by passing `profiles` and `review_example_cls` (or importing them module-scope), and keep parser helpers pure so they can be reused by other orchestration layers safely.

findings.summary: DSPy reviewer runtime failures are converted into successful reviewer completions.
evidence: `run_dspy_review` stores execution exceptions directly in results (`results[profile] = exc`).

`run_parallel_reviews_dspy` calls `prediction_to_review_output(prediction)` for each profile and increments `profiles_completed` unconditionally in the try path, even when prediction originated from an exception wrapper.
findings.suggestion: Treat `Exception` predictions as hard reviewer failures before conversion: set `review.error`, increment `profiles_failed`, and skip `parse_findings`/severity aggregation for that profile.

findings.summary: Aggregator computes a deduplicated set but publishes and scores raw duplicates.
evidence: Dedup loop creates `unique_findings` and increments `duplicates_removed` but `all_findings` is explicitly left unchanged.
Conflict detection and output serialization consume `aggregated.all_findings`, so duplicates still influence downstream interpretation and summary outputs.
findings.suggestion: Make dedup an explicit stage with selectable behavior: either replace `all_findings` with `unique_findings` for canonical outputs or expose separate fields (`all_findings_raw` and `all_findings_deduped`) and compute summaries from the chosen canonical list.

findings.summary: Default DSPy workflow depends on user-home skill directories outside the repo.
evidence: `SKILL_DIR` is hard-coded to `~/.claude/skills/fando-plan`, with optimized/training data resolved from that path.
CLI defaults to DSPy backend, making this non-repo path dependency active by default on machines with DSPy installed.
findings.suggestion: Move state path resolution behind explicit configuration (`--state-dir`/env var) with repository-local default, and keep home-directory path as opt-in compatibility mode.

findings.summary: Parallel review implementations disagree on empty-profile handling.
evidence: Codex path returns early for empty profile list.
DSPy path derives `max_workers=0` from empty profile list and passes it to `ThreadPoolExecutor`, which is invalid.
findings.suggestion: Add a shared guard at DSPy entry (`if not profiles: return {}`) and mirror that behavior in the higher-level wrapper to keep both backends behaviorally identical.

findings.summary: A single flat scripts folder mixes distinct domains and obscures ownership boundaries.
evidence: `fando-plan/scripts/` contains 12 files with heterogeneous concerns (aggregation, training backfill, CLI execution, profile detection), exceeding the mixed-concern flat-folder threshold.
Each file contains both reusable logic and executable CLI entrypoint, so folder placement reflects execution mode (`scripts`) rather than domain ownership.
Parallel verification scripts in `fando-verify/scripts/` repeat the same placement pattern instead of sharing a domain package.
findings.suggestion: Staged reorg plan: 1) create `fando_plan/review_core/` and move reusable logic from `aggregate_findings.py` and `call_codex.py`; create `fando_plan/training/` for `backfill_training.py` parsing/classification helpers. 2) create `fando_verify/core/` for diff/plan/parse helpers now in `find_plan.py`, `gather_implementation.py`, and `parse_verification.py`; keep thin CLIs under `fando-plan/scripts/` and `fando-verify/scripts/` that only parse args and call core APIs. 3) move files in order: pure helpers first, then wrapper CLIs; update imports with `rg "from .*scripts|import .*scripts" fando-plan fando-verify` and fix references. 4) validate with `python -m fando_plan.scripts.call_codex --check-only`, `python -m fando_verify.scripts.find_plan --list`, and `python -m compileall fando-plan fando-verify`.

findings.summary: Architecture is split by workflow phase instead of stable capabilities, increasing cross-phase drift.
evidence: Workflow-critical capabilities are distributed by phase-specific directories (`plan` vs `verify`) even though they compose one review pipeline.
`call_codex.py` and verify scripts each define their own process/result contracts (separate dataclasses and independent error/CLI patterns), creating multiple top-level conventions for one domain.
No single package-level API defines the end-to-end review/verification lifecycle; composition is implicit across standalone scripts.
findings.suggestion: Staged reorg plan: 1) introduce a shared capability package `fando_review/workflow/` with modules `plan_source.py`, `implementation_diff.py`, `codex_client.py`, `verification_parse.py`. 2) move logic from `find_plan.py` and `gather_implementation.py` first, then `call_codex.py` and `parse_verification.py`; retain existing script filenames as compatibility shims calling new APIs. 3) update imports and script entrypoints using `rg "from (fando-plan|fando-verify)\.scripts|import (find_plan|gather_implementation|call_codex|parse_verification)" -n`. 4) run validation commands: `python fando-plan/scripts/call_codex.py --check-only`, `python fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py --format=json`, `python fando-verify/scripts/gather_implementation.py --stat --format=json`, and `python fando-verify/scripts/parse_verification.py --summary-only < /tmp/sample_response.txt`.

findings.summary: Codex CLI boundary policy is duplicated across modules, causing contract drift risk.
evidence: `call_codex.py` owns capability probing and command construction (`verify_codex_cli`, `cmd=['codex','exec']`, optional `--skip-git-repo-check`).
`codex_lm.py` independently rebuilds execution/error contract (`cmd=['codex','exec']`, timeout, returncode handling), reusing only part of policy from `call_codex.py`.
README describes a stable Codex reviewer role, but the runtime boundary is split across ad-hoc implementations, making compatibility behavior inconsistent over time.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single `codex_runtime` module (for example `fando_core/codex_runtime.py`) that centralizes version/capability checks, command assembly, and error normalization; make both `call_codex.py` and `codex_lm.py` thin adapters over that API.

findings.summary: Compatibility and governance policy are documented but not enforced from one authoritative runtime contract.
evidence: README defines user-facing trust contract for Codex-backed workflows, but runtime scripts only check presence/flags and do not expose one shared compatibility gate.
`call_codex.py` does capability probing but no strict semantic version policy; `codex_lm.py` relies on same CLI but applies its own failure semantics.
Top-level decomposition in README is feature-centric while enforcement points are scattered in script internals, increasing ownership ambiguity for policy changes.
findings.suggestion: Define a single governance contract object (minimum supported CLI version, required capabilities, failure policy) and load it in both plan/verify flows; document this same contract in README so docs and runtime stay in lockstep.

findings.summary: Critical subprocess/git contract paths lack explicit verification strategy.
evidence: Core behavior depends on shelling out to `codex` and `git`, with multiple fallback branches and error paths.
No reviewed artifact describes or embeds contract tests for these branches (for example timeout behavior, missing binary, missing base branch, malformed remote URL).
Given these scripts are execution gateways, regressions in command parsing/fallback logic would directly impact plan/verify reliability.
findings.suggestion: Add staged quality gates: (1) unit tests with `subprocess.run` mocking for each failure mode, (2) fixture-based integration tests for git repo states, (3) CI command sequence such as `uv run pytest tests/fando_plan tests/fando_verify -q` plus a smoke test invoking each CLI in `--format=json` mode.

findings.summary: Flat `scripts/` layout mixes entrypoints and reusable runtime logic, obscuring ownership boundaries.
evidence: Structure signals show `fando-plan/scripts/` as a 12-file flat directory with script-only zoning, despite containing logic that is reused across modules.
`codex_lm.py` imports from another script file (`call_codex.py`), indicating runtime library behavior is living in entrypoint space.
README structure listing is incomplete versus active files, reducing navigational trust and reinforcing mismatch between physical layout and conceptual domains.
findings.suggestion: Staged reorg plan: Step 1 create `fando-plan/src/fando_plan/runtime/` and `fando-verify/src/fando_verify/runtime/`; Step 2 move reusable logic (`verify_codex_cli`, git/plan discovery helpers) into runtime modules and keep `scripts/` as thin CLIs; Step 3 update imports to package-qualified paths; Step 4 validate with `uv run python -m fando_plan.scripts.call_codex --check-only`, `uv run python -m fando_verify.scripts.find_plan --list --format=json`, and `uv run pytest -q`.

findings.summary: Core logic and CLI concerns are repeatedly collapsed into single modules.
evidence: run_parallel_reviews.py defines reusable orchestration functions and also owns CLI argument parsing, output formatting, and process exit policy.
dspy_reviewers.py combines domain Signature definitions, runtime orchestration, training-data serialization, optimization state load/save, and CLI status commands in one module.
parse_findings.py and parse_verification.py each mix parser logic with command-line IO/exit behavior, making parser reuse tightly coupled to shell workflow.
findings.suggestion: Split each script into `core` (pure functions/data models), `adapters` (Codex/DSPy/git/process integrations), and thin `cli` entrypoints. Keep CLI files limited to argparse + invoking core APIs so behavior can evolve without cross-cutting edits.

findings.summary: Two parallel review pipelines duplicate orchestration and aggregation responsibilities.
evidence: run_parallel_reviews.py implements both `run_parallel_reviews` (Codex path) and `run_parallel_reviews_dspy` (DSPy path), and both perform near-identical loops for per-profile results, parse_findings calls, and counter aggregation.
Codex invocation logic is split between `call_codex.py` and `codex_lm.py`, each building subprocess calls and error handling semantics separately for different call sites.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a single backend-agnostic reviewer runner interface (e.g., `ReviewerBackend.run(profile, plan) -> ReviewResult`) and one shared aggregation routine. Have Codex and DSPy backends implement only execution details.

findings.summary: Domain definitions are duplicated across modules instead of centralized.
evidence: detect_profiles.py owns `PROFILES` (keywords, display names, prompt files) while dspy_reviewers.py separately owns `DOMAIN_SIGNATURES` and related domain behavior.

backfill_training.py classifies findings by importing `PROFILES`, but optimize.py and runtime reviewer behavior are driven by `DOMAIN_SIGNATURES`, creating multiple sources of truth for what a domain is.
findings.suggestion: Create one domain registry module (domain id, labels, keyword sets, prompt/signature bindings, optimization eligibility) and import it everywhere to remove taxonomy drift.

findings.summary: Parsing modules embed workflow policy decisions that belong to orchestration.
evidence: parse_findings.py computes control-policy flags (`should_stop`, `stop_reason`) in addition to parsing tokens, which mixes interpretation policy with syntactic extraction.
run_parallel_reviews.py and aggregate_findings.py also compute readiness/outstanding policy (`has_outstanding_issues`) independently, creating overlapping decision layers.
findings.suggestion: Restrict parsers to structural extraction only (items/counts/errors) and move stop/approval policy into a dedicated orchestration policy module shared by plan and verification flows.

findings.summary: Template-cloned CLI wrappers are duplicated across scripts instead of using a shared runner.
evidence: Each file reimplements the same argparse + stdin read + empty-input error + output-format branching + exit-code logic rather than reusing a common CLI harness.
Behavior differs subtly between copies (error keys, stderr/text handling), increasing drift risk as scripts evolve.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared CLI utility module for input acquisition, format negotiation, and standardized error/exit handling; keep each script focused on domain parsing logic only.

findings.summary: Generated-style explanatory prose adds noise by restating obvious mechanics.
evidence: Large top-of-file Usage/Output blocks and in-function comments repeatedly explain straightforward operations (e.g., parsing section headers, reading stdin, counting matches) without documenting hidden constraints or invariants.
This pattern recurs in many files, making core logic harder to scan and increasing edit surface for non-functional text.
findings.suggestion: Trim comments/docstrings to intent and non-obvious constraints only; move repeated usage guidance to README or a shared docs section and keep function docs concise.

findings.summary: Async API is implemented as sync pass-through, adding interface ceremony without async behavior.
evidence: CodexLM.aforward() is declared async but directly returns self.forward(...), which still runs blocking subprocess.run().
The surrounding review pipeline already parallelizes at thread level, so this async surface is redundant and potentially misleading.
findings.suggestion: Either remove aforward() and keep a clearly sync LM adapter, or implement true async execution (async subprocess or executor) so interface and runtime behavior match.

findings.summary: LM response is overconstructed with synthetic metadata not aligned to actual return contract.
evidence: CodexLM.forward() builds a full chat-completion-like response dict with guessed token usage via split(), then returns only [output_text].
This creates extra generated-style scaffolding that is not consumed as a stable contract in this code path.
findings.suggestion: Return only the fields required by BaseLM/DSPy history and remove synthetic token accounting, or centralize a clearly typed minimal response schema used consistently.

findings.summary: DSPy execution failures can be misclassified as successful zero-finding reviews.
evidence: `prediction_to_review_output()` maps `Exception` to text (`## Findings` empty + `## Summary Error...`) instead of structured failure.
`run_parallel_reviews_dspy()` parses that text and increments `profiles_completed` before any semantic error check.
`parse_findings()` sets `should_stop=True` when HIGH/MEDIUM are zero, allowing failed reviewer runs to appear approval-equivalent.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a structured failure channel (`ReviewResult.error`) for prediction exceptions, skip findings parsing for failed predictions, and make `parse_findings` require explicit success markers before stop/approve decisions.

findings.summary: Module seam converts typed prediction state into text and re-parses it, increasing handoff fragility.
evidence: DSPy path emits structured prediction fields (`findings`, `summary`) but `run_parallel_reviews_dspy()` converts to markdown text and immediately regex-parses again.
This extra translation step creates avoidable mismatch risk between generation format and parser expectations.
findings.suggestion: Define a single internal `ParsedFindings` contract and build it directly from prediction fields; reserve markdown rendering for final display only.

findings.summary: Codex subprocess behavior is duplicated across modules with diverging contracts.
evidence: `call_codex.py` and `codex_lm.py` both implement command assembly, timeout handling, and returncode checks separately.
One path returns `CodexResult` with string errors while the other raises runtime exceptions, forcing callers to branch by source path.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared `codex_client` module with one invocation API (typed success/error result), then have both CLI and DSPy adapter depend on that single contract.

findings.summary: Core parser and orchestration decisions lack regression tests for malformed model output.
evidence: Both parser modules drive control flow via regex section extraction and category matching, but assigned scope shows no companion tests or fixtures.
`run_parallel_reviews.py` relies on these parsed counts for exit code and continuation decisions.
findings.suggestion: Add table-driven tests for parser edge cases (missing sections, mixed bullet styles, multiline items, exception summaries) and one integration test asserting failed-review outputs never produce approval/stop states.

findings.summary: Flat `scripts/` directories mix unrelated concerns and obscure ownership boundaries.
evidence: `fando-plan/scripts/` holds 12 files spanning runtime execution, parsing, profile detection, training data, optimization, and secret scanning.
`fando-verify/scripts/` mixes plan lookup, git diff collection, and verification parsing.
Holistic structure indicates script-centric flatness rather than capability packages.
findings.suggestion: Staged reorg plan: Stage 1 create `fando_plan/runtime`, `fando_plan/review`, `fando_plan/training`, `fando_verify/discovery`, `fando_verify/diff`, `fando_verify/parsing`; Stage 2 move files in this order: parsers (`parse_findings.py`, `parse_verification.py`) -> codex/runtime (`call_codex.py`, `codex_lm.py`, `run_parallel_reviews.py`) -> training/optimization (`collect_training.py`, `backfill_training.py`, `dspy_reviewers.py`, `optimize.py`) -> verification utilities (`find_plan.py`, `gather_implementation.py`); Stage 3 update imports using `rg "from (call_codex|parse_findings|dspy_reviewers|find_plan|gather_implementation)" -n`; Stage 4 validate with `python -m compileall fando-plan fando-verify` and smoke commands `python fando-plan/scripts/run_parallel_reviews.py --check-only` and `python fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py --list`.

findings.summary: Training example labeling mixes diffing, heuristic scoring, and dataset policy in one path.
evidence: `collect_training_example()` does extraction, diff generation, significance filtering, threshold scoring (>0.3), and label assignment in one function.
`backfill_training.py` separately infers domain/labels from historical logs with different assumptions, producing parallel policy surfaces.
findings.suggestion: Split labeling into explicit components (`finding_extractor`, `plan_diff_analyzer`, `label_policy`) and centralize threshold/policy constants in one module used by both live collection and backfill paths.
